the garden of eden story 2 (genesis 2 - 3) life knowledge day 2

god planted a garden in the east, in eden. there he put the man whom he had formed from the soil & he breathed his life - giving breath into him & the man began to live. god realized that it was not good for the man to live alone, so he decided to make a companion for him. then god brought all the birds and animals to the man and told him to give names to all of them.

then god put man into a deep sleep and as he slept, god took one of the man's ribs. god formed a woman out of the rib and brought her to him. the man and the woman were naked, but they were not ashamed.

1.the snake was the most cunning animal that god had made. 2. the snake tempted the woman to eat the fruit from the tree of knowledge. 3. the snake lied and said that, if they ate the fruit from the tree of knowledge, they would be like god, knowing everything.

the woman was tempted & saw that the fruit looked delicious. she forgot god's command, ate it and gave some to the man as well. when they ate the fruit, they disobeyed god's command, and sin entered the world. they were given understanding and realized that they were naked, so they covered themselves with leaves

when god came to walk in the garden, they hid from him because they were afraid, they were naked. god questioned them about eating from the forbidden tree, and adam blamed eve, while eve blamed the snake. god then gave consequences: pain in childbirth for eve, toil in work for adam and cursed the snake to crawl on its belly.

now man is like one of us, knowing all things. he must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree of life and live forever adam named his wife eve, because she was the mother of all human beings. god made clothes out of animal skins for adam and eve. then god sent them out of the garden of eden & told adam to till the soil from which he was made.
then at the east side of the garden, god put a living creature and a flaming sword. this was to keep anyone from coming near the tree that gives life.

story 4 (genesis 6 - 9) noah & the ark day 4

the human race slowly spread all over the world. however, they all started to become wicked, fostering only evil thoughts in their minds and hearts. due to all of this, god was filled with regret for creating man and all living beings. he decided to wipe out everything he had created. however, god was pleased with noah and wanted to save him.

noah had no faults and was the only good man of his time. he had 3 sons, shem, ham and japheth. god decided to destroy everything with a flood but he wanted to save noah. he told him to build an ark. then, noah built an ark and did everything as god had instructed him to do. build a boat for yourself with rooms in it, for i am going to send a flood to destroy everything

when the ark was completed, god told noah to take his family and a male and female of each species of all the birds and animals into the ark then, god closed the door of the ark, and after 7 days, the rain began to fall. the flood continued for 40 days, and the water became deep enough for the boat to float. the water covered the highest mountains.

the whole earth was covered with water. everything on earth that breathed died. the only ones left were noah, his family and the birds and animals, who were inside the ark. after 40 days, the rain stopped and the water gradually went down. then, noah sent out a dove to see if the land was dry.

the dove returned with an olive leaf, showing that the water had gone down and plants were growing again. when it was safe to leave the ark, god told noah to come out with his family and the animals. god told all of them to multiply and spread all over the earth. then, noah built an altar to thank god for keeping them safe.

noah offered a burnt sacrifice and prayed to god. god was pleased with noah and he made a promise to noah that he would never again flood the whole earth. as a sign of this promise, god placed a beautiful rainbow in the sky. the rainbow is a reminder of the covenant between god and us.

story 6 (genesis 12 - 18) abraham and his decendants day 6

abram & lot abram was a good and faithful man who loved and trusted god. he lived with his wife sarai and his nephew lot. abram and lot were wealthy and had plenty of land and cattle. however, there were frequent quarrels between the men of abram and lot. due to which, both decided to divide the land and live separately. abram rescues lot after few days, few kings attacked lot's land and robbed him of all his wealth. abram heard about this and went to rescue lot. abram fought those kings with his men, won against them, and brought back everything that was taken.

god's promise to abram abram and his wife sarai had no children. one night, god made a special promise to abram. he told abram that he would have as many descendants as the stars in the sky. sarai & hagar sarai was sad because she had no children. she asked abram to have a child with her servant, hagar. abram and hagar had a son named ishmael.

a new name & a new promise then god changed abram's name to abraham, as he was going to make him the ancestor of many nations. god also changed sarai's name to sarah, as she would become the mother of many nations. even though abraham and sarah were very old, god promised them a son. nine months later, they had a baby boy named isaac. god told them to start a new tradition: every baby boy should be circumcised at eight days old to show they were part of god’s promise.

the destruction of sodom & gomorrah story 7 (genesis 19) day 7
the cities of sodom and gomorrah were filled with wickedness. seeing their evil deeds, god decided to destroy them. however, abraham’s nephew lot, lived in sodom, and he was a righteous man.
god sent two angels to warn lot. they arrived in sodom and were welcomed into lot’s home. the angels told lot that the cities would be destroyed and urged him to take his family and flee.

the next morning , the angels told lot to leave quickly. "take your wife and daughters and flee! do not look back or stop anywhere in the valley. escape to the mountains, or you will be swept away!" lot hesitated, but the angels seized his hand, along with the hands of his wife and daughters, and led them out of the city safely. as they fled, the angels told them, "escape for your life! do not look back!" once lot and his family were out of sodom, god rained down fire and brimstone from the sky. sodom and gomorrah were utterly destroyed due to their immense wickedness. everything in the cities was consumed by fire.
lot's wife disobeyed the angel's warning and looked back at the city. as a result, she was turned into a pillar of salt. lot and his daughters continued to the mountains and reached safety.

story 8 (genesis 22) god tests abraham day 8

god decided to test abraham's faith and obedience. he called out to abraham, who immediately responded, "here i am." god then told abraham to go on a mountain and sacrifice his son to him. despite the painful request, abraham obeyed god without hesitation.

early the next morning abraham cut some wood for the sacrifice, loaded his donkey and took isaac and two servants with him. they traveled for three days until abraham saw the mountain in the distance. abraham told his servants to stay behind while he and isaac went up the mountain to worship.

when they reached the place god had told him about, abraham built an altar and arranged the wood on it. isaac asked abraham about the lamb for the sacrifice and he told isaac that god would provide the lamb. then abraham tied up isaac and placed him on the altar, on top of the wood .

just as abraham took the knife to sacrifice his son, the angel of the lord called out to him from heaven. the angel told abraham not to sacrifice isaac. then abraham saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. he went over, took the ram, and sacrificed it as a burnt offering instead of his son.

afterwards, the angel of the lord called to abraham a second time and said, "because you have done this and have not withheld your only son, i will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore. your descendants will take possession of the cities of their enemies, and through your offspring, all nations on earth will be blessed because you have obeyed me."

isaac and his descendants story 9 (genesis 23 - 35 ) day 9

genesis 23: the death of sarah sarah, abraham’s wife, passed away at 127 years old. abraham was very sad and wanted to find a special place to bury her. he bought a cave from the hittites and buried sarah there. genesis 24: isaac and rebekah abraham wanted a good wife for his son isaac. he sent his servant to his old home to find one. the servant prayed and found rebekah, who was kind and generous. she agreed to marry isaac, and they lived happily together.

genesis 26: isaac and abimelech isaac faced a famine and moved to a place called gerar. he told people rebekah was his sister because he was scared, just like abraham did with sarah. god blessed isaac, and he became very rich. the people of gerar were jealous, but isaac made peace with their king, abimelech. genesis 25: abraham’s death and descendants abraham married again and had more children, but he gave everything he owned to isaac. abraham died at 175 years old and was buried next to sarah. isaac’s wife, rebekah, had twins named esau and jacob. god told her that the older twin (esau) would serve the younger twin (jacob).

genesis 27: jacob and esau’s blessing isaac was old and blind and wanted to bless esau, his firstborn. rebekah and jacob tricked isaac into blessing jacob instead. esau was very angry and planned to hurt jacob, so jacob ran away to his uncle laban’s house. genesis 28: jacob’s dream at bethel on his way to his uncle’s house, jacob had a dream. he saw a ladder reaching to heaven with angels going up and down. god promised to bless jacob and give him many descendants. jacob promised to worship god and give back a tenth of everything god gave him.

genesis 35: jacob returns to bethel god told jacob to go back to bethel and build an altar. jacob obeyed, and god promised to bless him. rachel had another son, benjamin, but she died during childbirth. isaac also died, and jacob and esau buried him. jacob’s family continued to grow, just as god had promised.

joseph and his brothers story 10 (genesis 37 - 41) day 10

jacob continued to live in the land of canaan, where his father had lived. jacob's youngest son joseph, took care of the sheep and goats along with his brothers. he brought bad reports to his father about what his brothers were doing. jacob had twelve sons, but he loved his son joseph the most and gave him a special robe to wear. when his brothers saw that their father loved joseph more than he loved them, they hated their brother so much that they would not speak to him in a friendly manner. joseph had two dreams that made his brothers even angrier.

in one dream, his brother's sheaves of grain bowed down to his sheaf. in another dream, the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowed down to him these dreams suggested that joseph would one day rule over his family.

one day, jacob sent joseph to check on his brothers who were tending their flocks. when the brothers saw joseph coming, they plotted to kill him. however, reuben, the oldest brother, convinced them to throw joseph into a dry well instead, planning to rescue him later. when joseph came up to his brothers, they took him and threw him into the well, which was dry. while they were eating, they suddenly saw a group of ishmaelites travelling from gilead to egypt. they then thought to themselves that they would not gain anything by killing joseph, instead they could gain some money by selling him.

while reuben was away, the other brothers sold joseph to a caravan of ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver. when reuben came back to the well and found that joseph was not there, he tore his clothes in sorrow. he then went to his brothers and questioned them about everything.

as they approached the vineyards of timnah, suddenly a young lion came roaring toward him. the spirit of the lord came powerfully upon him so that he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as he might have torn a young goat. but he told neither his father nor his mother what he had done. then he went down and talked with the woman, and he liked her.

later, samson gave a riddle during a wedding feast, but the philistines pressured his wife into discovering the answer. after they solved the riddle dishonestly, samson became angry. then the spirit of the lord came powerfully upon him. he went down to ashkelon, struck down thirty of their men. he returned back home and samson’s wife was given to one of his companions at the feast.

the philistines later mistreated samson and his family, leading samson to take revenge against them. so, he went out and caught 300 foxes and tied them tail to tail in pairs. he then fastened a torch to every pair of tails, lit the torches and let the foxes loose in the standing grain of the philistines. he burned up the fields, vineyards and olive groves.

in retaliation, the philistines went up and burned samson's wife and her father to death. he attacked them viciously and slaughtered many of them. then he went down and stayed in a cave in the rock of etam.

later, when the philistines came to capture samson, the men of judah told that they would bring him. then three thousand men from judah went down to the cave in the rock of etam. then they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock. as he approached lehi, the philistines came toward him shouting.

the spirit of the lord came powerfully upon him. the ropes on his arms became like charred flax, and the bindings dropped from his hands. finding a fresh jawbone of a donkey, he grabbed it and struck down a thousand philistines. when he finished speaking, he threw away the jawbone; and the place was called ramath lehi.

because he was very thirsty, he cried out to the lord, “you have given your servant this great victory. must i now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?” then god opened up the hollow place in lehi, and water came out of it. when samson drank, his strength returned and he revived. samson led israel for twenty years in the days of the philistines.

samson eventually fell in love with a woman named delilah. the philistine rulers bribed delilah to discover the secret of samson’s great strength. they told her they would give her eleven hundred shekels of silver if she was able to tie him up and subdue him. so, delilah repeatedly began questioning him to find out the real reason of samson's strength. samson & delilah

1. samson answered, “if anyone ties me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, i’ll become as weak as any other man.” 2. then the rulers of the philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him with them. 3. with men hidden, she called to him, “samson, the philistines are upon you!” but he snapped the bowstrings easily. so the secret of his strength was not discovered.

1. he said, “if anyone ties me securely with new ropes that have never been used, i’ll become as weak as any other man.” 2. so, delilah took new ropes and tied him with them. 3. then, with men hidden in the room, she called to him, “samson, the philistines are upon you!” but he snapped the ropes off his arms as if they were threads.

1. he replied, “if you weave the seven braids of my head into the fabric on the loom and tighten it with the pin, i’ll become weak." 2. so, while he was sleeping, delilah took the seven braids of his head, wove them into the fabric and tightened it with the pin. 3. again she called to him, “samson, the philistines are upon you!” he awoke from his sleep and pulled up the pin and the loom, with the fabric.

with such nagging she prodded him day after day until he was sick to death of it. so, he told her everything that till date no razor was used on his head and if his head were shaved, his strength would leave him and he would become weak. after putting him to sleep on her lap, she called someone to shave off the seven braids of his hair, and his strength left him.

then she called, “samson, the philistines are upon you!” he awoke from his sleep and thought, “i’ll go out as before and shake myself free.” but he did not know that the lord had left him. then the philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes. binding him with bronze shackles, they set him to grinding grain in the prison. but later on, the hair on his head began to grow again after it had been shaved.

now the rulers of the philistines assembled to offer a great sacrifice to dagon their god and to celebrate their victory over samson. so they called samson out of the prison, and he performed for them. now the temple was crowded with men and women; all the rulers of the philistines were there, and on the roof were about 3000 men and women watching samson perform.

when they stood near him among the pillars, samson told the servant who was guiding him to take him near a pillar for support. then samson prayed to the lord to strengthen him to take revenge on the philistines. samson reached towards the 2 central pillars and pushed them. the temple came down on all the people in it. he killed many more when he died than while he lived.

give this a thought • samson defeated many philistines through the power god gave him, yet samson often used god’s gift selfishly and carelessly . even after many warnings, he continued making dangerous choices until delilah finally discovered the secret of his nazirite vow. samson’s downfall did not happen suddenly, it happened little by little through repeated compromise. sin often weakens people gradually before destroying them completely. are there areas in our lives where we are ignoring god’s warnings and falling into sin even after knowing that it is wro ng? • one of the saddest moments in samson’s life came when the bible says, “he did not know that the lord had left him.” samson still thought he could live in his own strength as before, but his disobedience had separated him from the fullness of god’s presence. this reminds us that spiritual pride is dangerous. are we truly staying close to god each day, or are we relying on our own strength? • even after samson failed greatly, god still listened when he sincerely cried out in repentance . though samson suffered the consequences of his sin, god mercifully gave him strength one final time to defeat israel’s enemies. can we learn from this that god can restore and use us again when we sincerely return to him?

story 23 (ruth 1 - 4) day 23 the life of ruth

during a time of famine in israel, a man named elimelek left bethlehem with his wife naomi and their two sons and moved to the land of moab. after some time, elimelek died, and naomi’s two sons married moabite women named orpah and ruth. later, both sons also died, leaving naomi alone with her daughters - in - law.

when naomi heard that the famine in israel had ended, she decided to return to bethlehem. naomi encouraged orpah and ruth to remain in moab, but ruth refused to leave naomi. naomi and ruth then returned together to bethlehem, arriving at the beginning of the barley harvest.

to provide food for herself and naomi, ruth went to gather leftover grain in the fields behind the harvesters. by god’s providence, she came to the field of boaz, a wealthy and kind relative of naomi’s late husband. boaz noticed ruth and learned about her loyalty and kindness toward naomi.

during mealtime, boaz invited ruth to sit with them and he offered her food. ruth gleaned in the field until evening. then she threshed the barley she had gathered, and it amounted to about an ephah. ruth returned home with abundant food, and naomi realized that boaz was one of their family redeemers who could help protect and provide for them.

naomi desired security and a future for ruth, so she told ruth to go to the threshing floor where boaz was working. ruth respectfully approached boaz at night and asked him to spread his garment over her. this would be a sign that he would become her family redeemer and care for her.

boaz promised to help her, though he explained that there was another relative who had a closer right to redeem the family property first. so, she lay at his feet until morning but got up before anyone could be recognized. before ruth returned home, boaz generously gave her grain to take back to naomi as a sign of his care and good intentions.

boaz went to the town gate and met the closer family redeemer before the elders of bethlehem. at first, the man agreed to redeem naomi’s land, but when he learned that he would also need to marry ruth and continue the family line, he refused because he feared it would affect his own inheritance. boaz then publicly agreed to redeem naomi’s family and marry ruth.

so, boaz took ruth and she became his wife. the elders blessed boaz and ruth, praying that their family would become great in israel. god blessed ruth and boaz with a son named obed, who later became the grandfather of king david.

give this a thought • the story of ruth begins during a time of famine, loss, and sorrow. naomi lost her husband and both of her sons, leaving her heart broken . yet in the middle of pain and uncertainty, ruth chose to remain faithful to naomi instead of returning to her own people. true love remains faithful not only in times of joy, but also in times of suffering and hardship. are we willing to remain faithful to god and to others even when life becomes difficult? • when boaz chose to redeem naomi’s family and marry ruth, god transformed their sorrow into joy and restoration . ruth, who had once been a foreign widow with no future, became part of god’s covenant people and was blessed abundantly. god gave ruth and boaz a son named obed, who became the grandfather of king david. through this family line, god eventually brought jesus christ into the world. this reminds us that god can bring beautiful restoration and purpose out of even the darkest situations. do we believe that god can still bring hope, healing , and restoration into our broken circumstances? or are we still stuc k down in our own sorrow?

story 24 (1 samuel 17) day 24 david & goliath

the philistines gathered their forces for war and assembled at sokoh in judah. saul & israelites assembled & camped in the valley of elah and drew up their battle line to meet the philistines. the philistines occupied one hill and the israelites another, with the valley between them.

a giant philistine warrior named goliath came out every day to challenge the israelites to send someone to fight him in a single combat. goliath was extremely tall and powerful, wearing heavy bronze armor and carrying massive weapons. for forty days, he mocked israel and insulted the god of israel, causing king saul and the israelite army to become fearful and discouraged.

meanwhile, david was a young shepherd boy who cared for his father jesse’s sheep in bethlehem. jesse’s three oldest sons had followed saul to the war. jesse sent david to bring food to his older brothers who were serving in saul’s army. early in the morning david left the flock in the care of a shepherd, loaded up and set out, as jesse had directed.

david left his things with the keeper of supplies, ran to the battle lines and asked his brothers how they were. when david arrived at the battlefield, he heard goliath mocking israel and was surprised that no one was willing to stand against him. david believed that the battle belonged to the lord and boldly declared that god would help defeat the giant.

king saul at first doubted david because he was young and inexperienced in battle. however, david explained how god had helped him protect his sheep from lions and bears. saul finally agreed to let david fight goliath. you are not able to go out against this philistine and fight him; you are only a young man, and he has been a warrior from his youth

then saul dressed david in his own tunic. he put a coat of armor on him and a bronze helmet on his head. but he refused saul’s heavy armor because he was not used to it. then he took his staff in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the stream, put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag and, with his sling in his hand, approached the philistine.

meanwhile, goliath kept coming closer to david. he looked at david and saw that he was little more than a boy, glowing with health and handsome, and he despised him. david was confident in the lord and he told goliath that god would give him victory so that everyone would know that there is a god in israel.

as goliath moved closer to attack him, david ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him. reaching into his bag and taking out a stone, he slung it and struck goliath on the forehead. the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.

david triumphed over the philistine with a sling and a stone. david ran and stood over him. he took hold of the philistine’s sword and drew it from the sheath. after he killed him, he cut off goliath's head with the sword. when the philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran. then the men of israel and judah surged forward with a shout and pursued the philistines.

when the israelites returned from chasing the philistines, they plundered their camp. david took goliath's head and brought it to jerusalem; he put goliath's weapons in his own tent. after the battle, david became famous throughout israel because god had given him victory over the giant.

give this a thought • when saul offered david his armor, david refused because he knew his victory would not come through human weapons or strength. instead, david stepped forward with a sling, a few stones, and complete trust in the lord. this teaches us that god does not need impressive abilities or perfect qualifications to accomplish his work. god delights in using humble and willing hearts that fully depend on him. reflect on this - are we relying on our own strength trying to do things alone, or are we trusting god completely in our battles? • david boldly declared that the battle belonged to the lord. his confidence was not in himself, but in god’s power and faithfulness. through one stone and simple obedience , god brought down the mighty giant and gave victory to israel. this reminds us that no giant in our lives is too great for god to overcome . fear, sin, suffering, discouragement, and impossible situations can all be defeated through faith in him. can we learn from this and begin to believe that only god alone is able to give victory over the giants we are facing today?

story 25 (1 kings 16 - 19) elijah & the prophets of baal day 25

israel continued to fall deeper into sin as many wicked kings ruled after jeroboam. kings like baasha, elah, zimri and omri led the people away from god & practiced evil eventually, omri's son ahab became king and was even more wicked than the kings before him. ahab married jezebel, the daughter of the king of sidon, and together they promoted the worship of baal throughout israel.

god raised up the prophet elijah to confront king ahab and the wickedness in israel. elijah said that there would be no rain in the land except by god’s word, bringing a severe drought upon israel. god then sent elijah to hide near the kerith ravine, where ravens brought him bread and meat each day. as the god of israel, lives, whom i serve, there will be neither dew nor rain in the next few years except at my word

later, when the brook dried up, god sent elijah to a widow in zarephath. so, he went to zarephath. when he came to the town gate, a widow was there gathering sticks. elijah asked her for water and a loaf of bread. she told him that she had very little flour and oil left in her house and that they were collecting sticks to make one last meal for themselves and then die of hunger.

elijah said to her, “don’t be afraid. go home and do as you have said. but first make a small loaf of bread for me from what you have and bring it to me and then make something for yourself and your son. she went away and did as elijah had told her. so, there was food every day for elijah and for the woman and her family. for the jar of flour was not used up and the jug of oil did not run dry.

some time later the son of the woman who owned the house became ill. he grew worse and worse, and finally stopped breathing. she said to elijah, “what do you have against me, man of god? did you come to remind me of my sin and kill my son?” “give me your son,” elijah replied. he took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying. he laid the boy on his bed. then he cried out to the lord, “lord my god, have you brought tragedy even on this widow i am staying with, by causing her son to die?” then he stretched himself out on the boy three times and cried out to the lord, “lord my god, let this boy’s life return to him!”

the lord heard elijah’s cry, and the boy’s life returned to him, and he lived. elijah picked up the child and carried him down from the room into the house. he gave him to his mother and said, “look, your son is alive!” then the woman said to elijah, “now i know that you are a man of god and that the word of the lord from your mouth is the truth.”

after three years of drought, god sent elijah to confront ahab again. he told ahab to send word throughout all israel and assemble all the prophets on mount carmel. elijah challenged the prophets of baal on mount carmel to prove whose god was truly powerful.

elijah told them to get 2 bulls. baal’s prophets had to choose one for themselves, cut it into pieces and put it on the wood but not set fire to it. then he would prepare the other bull and put it on the wood but not set fire to it. he told them to call on the name of god and whichever god would answer by fire, he would be the living god. they all agreed to do this.

so, they took the bull given them and prepared it. then they called on the name of baal from morning till noon. but there was no response. then they danced around the altar they had made. at noon elijah began to taunt them. "shout louder!" he said. "surely he is a god! perhaps he is deep in thought, or busy, or traveling." so, they shouted louder and slashed themselves with swords and spears.

then in the evening, elijah repaired the altar of the lord. elijah took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes descended from jacob. with the stones he built an altar in the name of the lord, and he dug a trench around it. he arranged the wood, cut the bull and laid it on the wood. he told few people to pour water on the offering.

then elijah prayed "answer me, lord, so that these people will know that you are god & that you are turning their hearts back again." then the fire of the lord fell and burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones and also licked up the water in the trench. when all the people saw this, they fell prostrate and cried, "the lord — he is god!" then elijah commanded them to seize the prophets of baal and kill them.

elijah told ahab to go to eat and drink as he went to pray to the lord for rain. elijah told his servant seven times to go and look at the sea for clouds and at the seventh time a small cloud rose from the sea. elijah told his servant to tell ahab to go back to jezreel as the sky grew black with clouds and heavy rain started falling.

on returning home, ahab told jezebel everything elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword. then queen jezebel threatened to kill elijah. afraid and discouraged, elijah fled into the wilderness and prayed that he might die. feeling lonely and exhausted, elijah rested under a broom tree, but god cared for him by sending an angel to give him food and water.

elijah traveled to mount horeb, where he experienced a powerful wind, an earthquake, and a fire, but the lord was not in them. then elijah heard a gentle whisper, and god spoke to him there. god reminded elijah that he was not alone and that there were still faithful people in israel. he told elijah to anoint jehu, king over israel and to anoint elisha to succeed him as prophet.

so elijah went from there and found elisha. he was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen. elijah went up to him and threw his cloak around him. then elisha went to say goodbye to his parents. he took his yoke of oxen and slaughtered them. he burned the plowing equipment to cook the meat and gave it to the people, and they ate. then he set out to follow elijah and became his servant.

give this a thought • the reign of ahab and jezebel reminds us how dangerous it is when people turn away from god and allow sin to rule their hearts. they promoted the worship of baal and led the nation of israel into deep spiritual darkness . yet even when evil seemed to spread everywhere, god still raised up elijah to stand boldly for truth . in our lives, are we truly standing firmly for god and his people or do we silently allow evil to have its own way? • elijah stood alone against hundreds of false prophets. while the prophets of baal cried out with no answer, god responded to elijah’s simple prayer by sending fire from heaven. the victory did not come through human power, but through faith and obedience . are we depending on god’s power, or are we placing our trust in human intervention & worldly things? • god reminded elijah that there were still faithful people serving him. then god gave elijah a new mission and called elisha to continue the prophetic work after him. this teaches us that god’s plans continue beyond one person, and he is always preparing others for his work. even when we feel small or discouraged, god can still use our lives for his greater purpose. each one of us has a calling and a purpose in life. have we identified our calling? if no, it's never too late.

elijah taken up to heaven story 26 (2 kings 2, 5) day 26 elisha & naaman

before elijah was taken to heaven, he and elisha traveled together from gilgal to bethel, jericho, and finally to the jordan river. elijah tested elisha several times by asking him to stay behind, but elisha faithfully refused to leave his master. fifty men from the company of the prophets went and stood at a distance, facing the place where elijah and elisha had stopped at the jordan. elijah taken up to heaven

elijah took his cloak, rolled it up and struck the water with it. the water divided to the right and to the left, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground. when they had crossed, elisha then asked elijah for a double portion of his spirit so that he could continue god’s work faithfully. elijah told him that he would receive it if he is able to see him being taken away.

as they continued walking together, a chariot of fire with horses of fire suddenly appeared and separated them. elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind while elisha watched in sorrow and amazement. then he took hold of his garment and tore it in two. elisha picked up elijah’s fallen cloak and returned to the jordan river.

he took the cloak that had fallen from elijah and struck the water with it. “where now is the lord, the god of elijah?” he asked. when he struck the water, it divided to the right and to the left, and he crossed over. the company of the prophets from jericho, who were watching, said, “the spirit of elijah is resting on elisha.” and they went to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

soon after, the people of jericho asked elisha to help because their water was bad and the land was unfruitful. “bring me a new bowl,” he said, “and put salt in it.” so they brought it to him. elisha threw salt into the spring, and god miraculously healed the water, making the land fruitful again. and the water has remained pure to this day, according to the word elisha had spoken.

now, naaman was the powerful commander of the army of aram, respected and honored by his king because through him the lord had given victory to aram. but he suffered from leprosy. a young israelite servant girl told naaman’s wife about the prophet elisha in israel who could heal him. naaman went to his master and told him what the girl from israel had said. elisha & naaman

so, he went down and dipped himself in the jordan seven times, as the man of god had told him, and his flesh was restored and became clean like that of a young boy.

story 27 (esther 1 - 10) day 27 the life of queen esther

king xerxes ruled over a vast persian empire and held a grand feast for many days in the capital city of susa. during the celebration, queen vashti refused to obey the king’s command to appear before his guests. because of this, the king became angry, and vashti was removed as queen.

later, young women from across the empire were brought to the palace so the king could choose a new queen. among them was esther, a beautiful jewish girl who had been raised by her cousin mordecai after her parents died. esther pleased the king greatly, and he chose her to become queen, though he did not know she was jewish.

one day mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate, two officers who guarded the doorway, conspired to assassinate king xerxes. but mordecai found out about the plot and told queen esther, who in turn reported it to the king, giving credit to mordecai. and when the report was found to be true, the two officials were impaled on poles. all this was recorded in the book of the annals.

meanwhile, a proud official named haman was promoted in the kingdom. haman became furious because mordecai refused to bow down to him. filled with hatred, haman planned not only to kill mordecai but also to destroy all the jewish people throughout the empire. he convinced the king to issue a decree ordering the jews to be destroyed on a certain day.

story 28 (job 1 - 3) day 28 the life of job (part 1)

in the land of uz there lived a man whose name was job. this man was blameless and upright; he feared god and shunned evil. he had seven sons and three daughters, and he owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred donkeys, and had a large number of servants. he was the greatest man among all the people of the east.

his sons used to hold feasts in their homes on their birthdays, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them. when a period of feasting had run its course, job would make arrangements for them to be purified. early in the morning he would sacrifice a burnt offering for each of them, thinking, “perhaps my children have sinned and cursed god in their hearts.” this was job’s regular custom.

one day the angels came to present themselves before the lord, and satan also came with them. the lord asked satan where he came from, and he told god that he was roaming the earth. then the lord said to satan, “have you considered my servant job? there is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears god and shuns evil.”

satan claimed that job only served god because he was blessed and protected. satan challenged god that if god would take everything job had, job would curse god. the lord said to satan, “very well, then, everything he has is in your power, but on the man himself do not lay a finger.” then satan went out from the presence of the lord.

while job’s children were gathered for a feast at the oldest brother’s house, a series of terrible disasters suddenly struck job one after another. first, the sabeans attacked and stole job’s oxen and donkeys, killing the servants who were caring for them. before the first messenger finished speaking, another reported that fire had fallen from heaven and destroyed job’s sheep and servants.

then another messenger came saying that the chaldeans had raided job’s camels and killed more servants. then the worst news - a mighty wind had struck the house where job’s sons and daughters were feasting. the house collapsed and killed all of them. in a single day, job lost everything through devastating events.

at this, job got up and tore his robe and shaved his head. then he fell to the ground in worship and said: “naked i came from my mother’s womb, and naked i will depart. the lord gave and the lord has taken away; may the name of the lord be praised.” in all this, job did not sin by charging god with wrongdoing.

on another day the angels came to present themselves before the lord and satan also came there. god told satan that job maintained his integrity, even though satan ruined him without any reason. but satan challenged god again, that job would curse god if his own life would be endangered. then god gave job into satan's hands but warned him to spare his life.

then satan afflicted job with painful sores all over his body. job took a piece of broken pottery and scraped himself with it as he sat among the ashes. his wife said to him, “are you still maintaining your integrity? curse god and die!” he replied, “you are talking like a foolish woman. shall we accept good from god, and not trouble?” in all this, job did not sin in what he said.

when job’s 3 friends, eliphaz, bildad and zophar heard about all the troubles that had come upon him, they went to comfort him. when they saw him from a distance, they began to weep aloud, & they tore their robes and sprinkled dust on their heads. then they sat on the ground with him for 7 days and 7 nights. no one said a word to him, because they saw how great his suffering was.

job defended his innocence and struggled to understand why he was suffering so deeply. he cried out to god, questioned his pain, and longed for answers. job wrestled with confusion, grief, loneliness, and disappointment, yet he still continued seeking god.
story 29 (job 4 - 42) day 29 the life of job (part 2)

then job's friends began arguing with job. they believed suffering only comes because of personal sin, so they insisted that job must have secretly done something wrong. they continued accusing him, saying that god only punishes the wicked and blesses the righteous. job, however, knew he had not turned away from god, though he admitted that no human being is completely pure before him.

the 3 men stopped arguing with job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. a younger man named elihu then spoke. elihu became very angry with job for justifying himself rather than god. he was also angry with the three friends, because they had found no way to refute job, and yet had condemned him.
elihu explained that god is greater than human understanding and that suffering can sometimes be used by god to teach, correct, and draw people closer to him.

finally, god himself spoke to job out of a whirlwind. instead of directly explaining job’s suffering, god revealed his greatness, wisdom, and power through creation. he asked job many questions about the earth, heavens, animals, and the mysteries of the universe, questions no human could answer. job realized how limited human understanding is compared to god’s infinite wisdom.

job humbled himself, repented for speaking without fully understanding, and worshiped god. god then rebuked job’s three friends because they had spoken wrongly about him. he instructed them to offer sacrifices, and job prayed for them. after job had prayed for his friends, the lord restored his fortunes and gave him twice as much as he had before.

all his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came and ate with him in his house. they comforted and consoled him over all the trouble the lord had brought on him. each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.

the lord blessed the latter part of job’s life more than the former part. he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand donkeys. and he also had seven sons and three daughters. the first daughter he named jemimah, the second keziah and the third keren - happuch.

nowhere in all the land were there found women as beautiful as job’s daughters, and their father granted them an inheritance along with their brothers. after this, job lived a hundred and forty years; he saw his children and their children to the fourth generation. and so, job died, an old man and full of years.

story 30 (daniel 1 - 3) day 30 the life of daniel

in the third year of the reign of jehoiakim king of judah, nebuchadnezzar king of babylon came to jerusalem & besieged it and the lord delivered jehoiakim king of judah into his hand, along with some of the articles from the temple. these he carried off to the temple of his god in babylonia and put in the treasure house of his god.

then the king ordered ashpenaz, chief of his court officials, to bring into the king’s service some of the israelites from the royal family and the nobility, young men without any physical defect, handsome, showing aptitude for every kind of learning, well informed, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace. he was to teach them the language and literature of the babylonians. the king assigned them a daily amount of food and wine from the king’s table. they were to be trained for three years, and after that they were to enter the king’s service.

among those who were chosen were some from judah: daniel, hananiah, mishael and azariah. but daniel resolved not to defile himself with the royal food and wine, and he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself this way. the official was afraid that daniel would look weaker than the other men if he didn't eat royal food and then the king would get angry.

daniel told the official to test them for 10 days by giving them vegetables and water. the official agreed and at the end of 10 days they looked healthier and better nourished than any of the young men who ate the royal food. so the official continued giving them vegetables. god blessed their faithfulness and gave them wisdom and understanding, and daniel received the ability to interpret dreams and visions.

in the second year of his reign, nebuchadnezzar had dreams; his mind was troubled and he could not sleep. so the king summoned all his wise men to tell him what he had dreamed. but he refused to tell the dream to his wise men, demanding that they both reveal the dream and interpret it. when they could not, he ordered all the wise men of babylon to be executed.

at this, daniel went in to the king and asked for time, so that he might interpret the dream for him. then daniel prayed with his friends. he pleaded for mercy from god concerning this mystery, so that he and his friends might not be executed with the rest of the wise men of babylon. during the night the mystery was revealed to daniel in a vision. then daniel praised the god of heaven.

daniel told the king about the dream - a great statue made of different metals: a head of gold, chest of silver, belly of bronze, legs of iron, and feet partly of iron and clay. a stone cut without human hands struck the statue and destroyed it. daniel explained that the statue represented successive kingdoms, while the stone was god’s eternal kingdom that would never be destroyed.

then king nebuchadnezzar fell prostrate before daniel and paid him honor. then the king placed daniel in a high position and lavished many gifts on him. he made him ruler over the entire province of babylon. moreover, at daniel’s request the king appointed shadrach, meshach and abednego administrators over the province of babylon, while daniel himself remained at the royal court.

nebuchadnezzar built a huge golden image and commanded everyone to bow down and worship it. daniel’s three friends refused to worship the image because they would worship only god. furious, the king ordered them thrown into a blazing furnace heated seven times hotter than usual.

so, these men were bound and thrown into the blazing furnace. then king nebuchadnezzar leaped to his feet in amazement and asked his advisers, “weren’t there three men that we tied up and threw into the fire?” they replied, “certainly, your majesty.” he said, “look! i see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods.”

nebuchadnezzar then approached the opening of the blazing furnace and told them to come out. everyone crowded around them. they saw that the fire had not harmed their bodies, their robes were not scorched, and there was no smell of fire on them. nebuchadnezzar praised god and issued a decree honoring the god of shadrach, meshach and abednego.
story 31 (daniel 4 - 6) day 31 daniel in the lion's den

nebuchadnezzar had another dream about a great tree, with abundant fruit and shelter for many animals & birds was cut down, leaving only the stump. daniel interpreted the dream and warned the king that because of his pride he would be driven away from people and live like an animal until he acknowledged that god rules over all kingdoms.

a year later, while boasting about his greatness, the prophecy was fulfilled. nebuchadnezzar lost his sanity and lived among the wild animals. he was driven away from people and ate grass like the ox. after a period of time, he humbled himself and acknowledged god’s sovereignty. his kingdom was restored, and he praised and honored the most high god.

many years later, king belshazzar held a great banquet and used the sacred gold and silver vessels that nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines might drink from them. as they drank the wine, they praised the gods of gold and silver, of bronze, iron, wood and stone.

suddenly the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall. the king watched the hand as it wrote. his face turned pale and he was so frightened that his legs became weak and his knees were knocking. the king called his wise men to explain it. then all the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or tell the king what it meant.

the queen suggested to call daniel to explain this. so daniel was brought before the king. the king offered daniel many gifts but daniel refused them. then he began explaining what the writing meant. he told the king that god's judgement was upon him because he did not humble himself unlike his father. he used the sacred vessels, drank wine from them and praised the gods of silver and gold.

the words "mene, mene, tekel, parsin" meant that god had numbered his days, weighed him and found him wanting, and that his kingdom would be given to the medes and persians. then daniel was given gifts, and he was proclaimed the third highest ruler in the kingdom. but that very night belshazzar was killed, and babylon fell to the medes and persians.

under the rule of king darius, daniel distinguished himself through his integrity and wisdom. jealous officials were searching for ways to accuse him, but they could not unless it was related to god. they convinced the king to issue a law that no one could pray to any god except the king for thirty days.

when daniel heard about the decree, he went to his upstairs room where the windows opened toward jerusalem. 3 times a day he got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to his god, just as he had done before. then these men went as a group and found daniel praying and asking god for help.

then the men went to king darius and said to him, “remember, that according to the law of the medes and persians no decree that the king issues can be changed.” they told the king that daniel was praying 3 times a day. so, the king gave the order, and they brought daniel and threw him into the lion's den. he told daniel, “may your god, whom you serve continually, rescue you!”

a stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring, so that daniel’s situation might not be changed. then the king returned to his palace and spent the night without eating and without any entertainment being brought to him. and he could not sleep. at the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the lions’ den.

when the king came near the den, he called to daniel in an anguished voice, “daniel, servant of the living god, has your god, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?” and daniel responded back, "my god sent his angel, and he shut the mouths of the lions. they have not hurt me, because i was found innocent in his sight. nor have i ever done any wrong before you, your majesty.”

the king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift daniel out of the den. at the king’s command, the men who had falsely accused daniel were thrown into the lions’ den, along with their wives and children. and before they reached the floor of the den, the lions crushed all their bones. the king then proclaimed throughout the kingdom that everyone should honor the god of daniel.

story 32 (jonah 1 - 4) jonah and the city of nineveh day 32

god called jonah, a prophet of israel, and commanded him to go to the great city of nineveh and preach against its wickedness. instead of obeying, jonah ran away from the lord and headed for tarshish. he went down to joppa, where he found a ship bound for that port. after paying the fare, he went aboard and sailed for tarshish to flee from the lord.

then the lord sent a great wind on the sea, and such a violent storm arose that the ship threatened to break up. all the sailors were afraid and each cried out to his own god. and they threw their cargo into the sea. but jonah had gone below deck, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.

the captain went to him and said, “how can you sleep? get up and call on your god! maybe he will take notice of us so that we will not perish.” then the sailors said to each other, “come, let us cast lots to find out who is responsible for this calamity.” they cast lots and the lot fell on jonah. they questioned jonah about few things & he admitted that he was fleeing from the lord.

the sea was getting rougher and rougher. then jonah told them that if they threw him into the sea, it would become calm. the men did their best to row back to land. but the sea grew even wilder than before. at jonah’s request, the sailors threw him into the sea, and immediately the storm became calm. at this the men greatly feared the lord, and they offered a sacrifice to the lord.
now the lord provided a huge fish to swallow jonah, and jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

from inside the fish jonah prayed to the lord his god. he acknowledged that god had saved him from death and thanked him for his mercy. jonah promised to obey the lord and declared that salvation comes from god alone.

the lord commanded the fish, and it vomited jonah onto dry land. the word of the lord came to jonah a second time, telling him again to go to nineveh. this time jonah obeyed and traveled to the city. nineveh was a large city and it took three days to go through it.

jonah began by going a day’s journey into the city, proclaiming, “forty more days and nineveh will be overthrown.” the ninevites believed god. a fast was proclaimed, and all of them, from the greatest to the least, put on sackcloth. when jonah’s warning reached the king of nineveh, he rose from his throne, took off his royal robes, covered himself with sackcloth and sat down in the dust.

from the greatest to the least, they repented, fasted, and wore sackcloth as a sign of sorrow for their sins. even the king humbled himself, sat in ashes, and called for everyone to turn away from their evil ways. when god saw their genuine repentance, he showed mercy and did not bring the destruction he had announced.

instead of rejoicing, jonah became angry because god had spared nineveh. he complained that this was why he had tried to flee in the first place knowing that god is gracious & merciful. then jonah left the city and sat outside it, hoping to see what would happen.

god caused a plant to grow and provide shade for jonah, making him very happy but at dawn the next day god provided a worm, which chewed the plant so that it withered. god sent a scorching east wind caused jonah great discomfort. jonah became upset and wished to die.

god used the plant to teach jonah an important lesson. jonah cared deeply about a plant that he had not planted or nurtured, yet he showed no compassion for the people of nineveh. god reminded jonah that nineveh contained more than 120,000 people who did not know right from wrong, as well as many animals. through this, god revealed his desire that sinners repent rather than perish. you have been concerned about this plant, though you did not tend it or make it grow. and should i not have concern for nineveh?

story 33 (tobit 1 - 12) day 33 the life of tobit & tobias

tobit was a faithful israelite living in exile in nineveh. even though many of his fellow israelites abandoned god's laws, tobit remained devoted to god. he generously helped the poor and courageously buried fellow israelites who had been killed.

because of his faithfulness, he faced many hardships and eventually became blind after an accident involving bird droppings falling into his eyes. his blindness left him unable to work, and he suffered greatly while remaining faithful to god. as tobit's suffering continued, he became deeply discouraged and prayed to god for mercy.

when tobias and sarah were married, everyone feared that tobias would suffer the same fate as the others. however, tobias obeyed raphael's instructions and placed the fish's heart and liver on burning incense. as the smoke rose, the demon asmodeus fled far away into egypt. raphael chased after him and caught him there. at once he bound him hand and foot.
