when jesus arrived in bethany, lazarus had already been in the tomb for four days. martha went out to meet him and expressed her sorrow that her brother had died, but she still trusted in jesus. jesus comforted her by declaring, “i am the resurrection and the life,” teaching that everyone who believes in him will have eternal life. martha confessed her faith that jesus was the messiah, the son of god.

mary then came to jesus and overcome with grief, fell at his feet. seeing mary, her friends, and the mourners weeping, jesus was deeply moved and also wept. he then went to the tomb, which was sealed with a large stone.

jesus ordered the stone to be removed despite martha’s concern that lazarus had been dead for four days. after thanking the father in prayer, jesus called out with a loud voice. immediately lazarus came out of the tomb alive, still wrapped in his burial cloths. jesus instructed the people to remove the grave clothes and let him go free. after seeing this miracle, many believed in him.

one day, as jesus was passing through jericho, a wealthy chief tax collector named zacchaeus wanted to see him. because he was short and could not see over the crowd, he climbed a sycamore tree along the road where jesus would pass. when jesus reached the tree, he looked up and said to him, "zacchaeus, hurry and come down; for i must stay at your house today." ( luke 19)

all who saw it began to grumble and said, "he has gone to be the guest of one who is a sinner." zacchaeus said, "lord, i will give half of my possessions to the poor and if i have defrauded anyone, i will pay back four times as much." then jesus said to him, "today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of abraham. for the son of man came to seek out and to save the lost."
the week of the passover story 45 (read john 12, luke 19:28 - 48, 21) day 45

six days before the passover jesus came to bethany, the home of lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead. there they gave a dinner for him. martha served, and lazarus was one of those at the table. mary took a pound of costly perfume made of pure nard, anointed jesus' feet, and wiped them with her hair. the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume. ( john 12)

but judas iscariot said, "why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?" (he said this not because he cared about the poor, but because kept the common purse and used to steal from it) jesus said, "leave her alone. she bought it so that she might keep it for the day of my burial. you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me."

the next day when they were near jerusalem and had reached the mount of olives, jesus sent two disciples, saying to them, "go into the village ahead of you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her; untie them and bring them to me. if anyone says anything to you, just say this, "the lord needs them.' and he will send them immediately. " this took place to fulfill what had been spoken through the prophet, saying, "tell the daughter of zion, look, your king is coming to you, humble, and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, the foal of a donkey." the disciples went and did as jesus had directed them; they brought the donkey and the colt, and put their cloaks on them, and he sat on them.

a large crowd spread their cloaks on the road, and others cut branches and spread them on the road. the crowds that followed him were shouting, "hosanna to the son of david! blessed is the one who comes in the name of the lord!" when he entered jerusalem, the whole city wanted to know who jesus was. the crowds were saying, "this is the prophet jesus from nazareth in galilee."

after entering jerusalem, jesus went to the temple and found merchants and money changers conducting business. filled with zeal for god’s house, he drove them out, overturned their tables, and rebuked them for turning a place of worship into a marketplace. jesus reminded them that the temple was meant to be a house of prayer, not a place of greed and corruption.

every day he was teaching in the temple. the chief priests kept looking for a way to kill him, but they did not find anything they could do, for all the people were spellbound by what they heard. he looked up and saw rich people putting their gifts into the treasury, he also saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins. he told them that her gift was greater than all others as she gave all she had to live on.
judas betrays jesus & the last supper story 46 (read luke 22, john 13 - 17) day 46

as the feast of unleavened bread, also called the passover, approached, the chief priests and scribes secretly searched for a way to kill jesus but feared the people. then satan entered into judas called iscariot, who was one of the twelve; he approached the chief priests and agreed to betray jesus in exchange for 30 silver pieces and began looking for the right opportunity.

on the day the passover lamb was to be sacrificed, jesus sent peter and john to prepare the passover meal. he told them they would meet a man carrying a jar of water, who would lead them to a large furnished upper room where they could make everything ready. they found everything exactly as jesus had said and prepared the passover meal.

when the time came, jesus gathered with his apostles in the upper room. then he poured water into a basin and began to wash all his disciples' feet and to wipe them with the towel that was tied around him. peter at first refused but, jesus explained that this act symbolized spiritual cleansing and that his followers should serve one another with the same love and humility. ( john 13)

after this jesus declared, "very truly, i tell you, one of you will betray me." the disciples looked at one another, uncertain of whom he was speaking. peter then motioned to john who was near jesus to ask him of whom he was speaking. so, he asked jesus who it was. jesus told him, it would be the one to whom he would dip the bread & give. so, he dipped the piece of bread and gave it to judas iscariot.

then, satan entered into judas. jesus said to him, "do quickly what you are going to do." now no one at the table knew why he said this to him. jesus gave his disciples a new commandment: to love one another just as he had loved them, saying that this love would identify them as his followers. jesus also told peter that although he desired to remain faithful, before the rooster crowed he would deny jesus three times.

then he took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, "this is my body, which is given for you. do this in remembrance of me." in the same way, he took the cup after supper, saying, "this cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood." the institution of the eucharist
the agony in the garden & the arrest of jesus story 47 (read matthew 26:36 - 75) day 47

then, jesus went with his disciples to the garden of gethsemane, where he prayed in deep sorrow before his suffering. taking peter, james, and john, he asked them to stay awake and pray. jesus went a little farther and threw himself on the ground and prayed to his heavenly father. jesus prayed three times, submitting himself completely to the father's will. the agony in the garden

but each time he returned, he found them asleep. he woke them & said to peter, "so, could you not stay awake with me for one hour? stay awake and pray that you may not come into the time of trial; the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak." when he returned to them the third time, he woke them and alerted them that the betrayer had arrived & he was going to be arrested.

soon judas arrived with a crowd of soldiers and temple guards, identifying jesus with a kiss. jesus was arrested, and although one disciple tried to defend him with a sword jesus stopped the violence, knowing that god's plan had to be fulfilled. the disciples then fled in fear.

jesus was taken to the house of caiaphas, where the chief priests searched for false witnesses to condemn him. although many accusations were made, jesus remained silent until he declared that he was the messiah, the son of god. the high priest accused him of blasphemy, and the council condemned him to death. they mocked him, spat on him, struck him, and insulted him.

meanwhile, peter followed from a distance into the high priest's courtyard. there, three different people recognized him as one of jesus' followers, but each time peter denied knowing jesus. immediately after his third denial, a rooster crowed. peter remembered what jesus had said to him. filled with sorrow and remorse, peter went away and wept bitterly.
the passion of jesus christ story 48 (read matthew 27) day 48

when morning came, the chief priests and elders handed jesus over to the roman governor, pilate, so that he could be condemned to death. judas, filled with remorse for betraying jesus, returned the thirty pieces of silver to the religious leaders, confessed his sin, and then took his own life. the priests used the money to buy the potter’s field, fulfilling the words of the prophet.

now jesus stood before pilate and pilate asked him, "are you the king of the jews?" jesus said, "you say so." but when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he did not answer. then pilate said to him, "do you not hear how many accusations they make against you?" but he gave him no answer, not even to a single charge, and pilate was greatly amazed.

now at the festival pilate was accustomed to release a prisoner for the crowd, anyone whom they wanted. pilate recognized jesus's innocence, but the crowd & religious leaders demanded the release of barabbas and cried out for jesus to be crucified. pilate symbolically washed his hands of the matter, and jesus was handed over to be flogged and crucified.
then the soldiers of pilate took jesus into the praetorium and began to scourge him. they stripped him of his clothes, tied him to a pillar and beat him using whips. the scourging at the pillar

after scourging him, they put a scarlet robe on h im, and after twisting some thorns into a crown, they put it on his head. they put a reed in his hand and knelt before him and mocked him, saying, "hail, king of the jews!" they spat on him and took the reed and struck him on the head. after mocking him, they stripped him of the robe and put his own clothes on him. then they led him away to crucify him. the crowning with thorns
in the morning, jesus was given his cross to carry towards golgotha (which means place of a skull). on the way, simon of cyrene was forced to help jesus carry his cross. the carrying of the cross

when they reached golgotha, they crucified him & divided his clothes among themselves by casting lots. over his head they put the charge against him, which read, "jesus of nazareth, king of the jews." then two thieves were crucified with him. the soldiers and crowds continued to mock him. when he was thirsty, they filled sour wine in a sponge and gave him.

from noon on, darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon. about three o'clock jesus cried out with a loud voice, "my god, my god, why have you forsaken me?" when some of the bystanders heard it, they said, "this man is calling for elijah." the other thief repented and asked jesus for mercy and jesus granted him eternal life.

meanwhile, standing near the cross of jesus were his mother, and mary the wife of clopas, mary magdalene and john. when jesus saw his mother and john, he said to his mother, "woman, here is your son." then he said to john, "here is your mother." and from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.

then jesus cried again with a loud voice, he bowed his head and gave up his spirit into the hands of his heavenly father. at that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two. the earth shook, and the rocks were split. the tombs also were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised. the death of jesus

the jews did not want the bodies left on the cross during the sabbath. so, they asked pilate to have the legs of the crucified men broken and the bodies removed. then the soldiers broke the legs of both thieves. but when they came to jesus & saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs. instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood & water came out. ( john 19:31 - 34)

that evening, there came a rich man from arimathea, named joseph who courageously asked pilate for jesus’ body. he wrapped jesus in a clean linen cloth and laid him in a new tomb. mary magdalene was sitting opposite to it. the chief priests asked pilate to secure the tomb as they remembered jesus’ promise of him rising after 3 days.
the resurrection of jesus story 49 (read luke 24) day 49

then the angels reminded them that jesus had foretold his death and resurrection. the women hurried back and told the apostles, b ut they did not believe them. but peter got up and ran to the tomb; stooping and looking in, he saw the linen cloths by themselves; then he went home, amazed at what had happened. early on the first day of the week, mary magdalene, joanna, mary the mother of james, and the other women went to jesus’ tomb with spices. they found the stone rolled & the tomb empty. suddenly, two angels appeared and announced that jesus had risen saying, "why do you look for the living among the dead? he is not here, but has risen."

later, two disciples were walking to the village of emmaus. the risen jesus joined them, but they did not recognize him. as they walked, jesus explained how the scriptures from moses and the prophets had foretold that the messiah had to suffer and then enter into his glory. when they reached emmaus, jesus blessed and broke the bread during their meal. at that moment, their eyes were opened, they recognized him, and he disappeared from their sight. filled with joy, they immediately returned to jerusalem to tell the other disciples.

while the disciples were gathered together, jesus suddenly stood among them and greeted them, saying, “peace be with you.” though they were frightened, thinking they had seen a ghost, jesus showed them his hands and feet, invited them to touch him. he then opened their minds to understand the scriptures, explaining that his suffering, death, and resurrection fulfilled god's plan. he commanded them to proclaim repentance and forgiveness of sins to all nations and promised to send them the holy spirit.

then he led them out as far as bethany and lifting up his hands, he blessed them. while he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and ascended into heaven. they worshiped him. then, they returned to jerusalem with great joy, and they were continually in the temple blessing god. the ascension of jesus
the birth of the church story 50 (read acts 1 - 3) day 50

after jesus ascended into heaven, the apostles returned to jerusalem from the mount of olives and gathered together in the upper room where they were staying. along with mary, the mother of jesus, other faithful women, and jesus' brothers, they devoted themselves to constant prayer, waiting for the promise of the holy spirit. during this time, peter addressed the disciples, explaining that the scriptures had foretold judas iscariot's betrayal and that his place among the apostles needed to be filled. two faithful disciples, joseph barsabbas (justus) and matthias, were chosen as candidates. after praying for god's guidance, they cast lots, and matthias was chosen to become the twelfth apostle.

the descent of the holy spirit then, on pentecost, all disciples gathered in one place. suddenly, a mighty sound like a rushing wind filled the house. divided tongues, as of fire, appeared among them, and a tongue rested on each of them. all of them were filled with the holy spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the spirit gave them ability.

at that time, jews from many nations were in jerusalem, and they were astonished to hear the disciples proclaiming god's mighty works in their own native languages. and at this sound the crowd gathered and were amazed and wondered what this miraculous event meant, while some mocked the disciples, wrongly accusing them of being drunk.

then, peter stood with the 11 apostles and boldly addressed the large crowd in jerusalem. he explained that the disciples were not drunk, but that the miraculous events were the fulfillment of joel's prophecy that god would pour out his spirit upon all people in the last days. peter then proclaimed that jesus of nazareth, whom the people had rejected and crucified, was the promised messiah. peter's message deeply touched the hearts of many in the crowd, and they asked what they should do. peter urged them to repent, be baptized in the name of jesus christ for the forgiveness of their sins and receive the gift of the holy spirit. about three thousand people believed and were baptized that day, marking the rapid growth of the early church.

the new christians devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread, and prayer. they lived in unity, shared their possessions with those in need, worshipped & praised god together daily. as they faithfully lived out their faith, the lord continued adding people to the church every day.

one day, peter and john went to the temple for the afternoon prayer. at the temple gate they met a man who had been lame from birth & begged for alms daily. when he saw peter and john about to go into the temple, he asked them for alms. looking at him with compassion, peter said, "i have no silver or gold, but what i have i give you; in the name of jesus christ of nazareth, stand up and walk."

taking the man by the hand, peter helped him up, and immediately his feet and ankles were completely healed. the man began walking, leaping & praising god as he entered the temple. everyone recognized him as the man who had always begged at the gate, and they were filled with amazement and wonder at the miraculous healing that god had performed through the name of jesus christ.
ananias & sapphira & stephen's martyrdom story 51 (read acts 5 - 7) day 51

as soon as ananias heard peter's words, he fell down and died. the young men wrapped his body, carried him out, and buried him, and great fear spread among everyone who heard what had happened. among the early christians, a man ananias & his wife sapphira, sold a piece of land. although they had agreed to give the proceeds to god, they secretly kept back part of the money while pretending to offer the full amount to the apostles. filled with the holy spirit, peter confronted ananias, explaining that he had not lied to people but to god by deceitfully testing the holy spirit.

about three hours later, sapphira arrived, unaware of her husband's fate. peter asked her whether the amount they had given was the full price of the land, and she repeated the same lie. peter rebuked her for joining her husband in testing the spirit of the lord and told her that the men who had buried ananias were at the door and would also carry her out. immediately, sapphira fell dead at peter's feet. the young men carried her out and buried her beside her husband. this powerful event filled the entire church and all who heard about it with great fear, reminding the early christians that god is holy, truthful, and desires sincere hearts rather than outward appearances or deception.

stephen, a man full of god's grace, wisdom, and the holy spirit, performed many miracles and boldly preached about jesus. his powerful teaching angered some religious leaders from various synagogues, but they could not overcome the wisdom and truth with which he spoke. as everyone looked at him, they saw that his face shone like the face of an angel, reflecting god's presence.

then, stephen was arrested and brought before the jewish council. standing before the council, stephen delivered a powerful sermon, recounting israel's history from abraham, joseph, moses, the exodus, the wilderness, joshua, david, and solomon, showing how god had faithfully guided his people throughout history. he reminded them that their ancestors repeatedly rejected god's chosen servants, including moses and the prophets, and concluded by boldly declaring that they had likewise rejected and crucified jesus, the promised messiah. stephen accused them of resisting the holy spirit just as their ancestors had done.

enraged by his words, the members of the council became furious. filled with the holy spirit, stephen looked up into heaven and saw the glory of god and jesus standing at the right hand of the father. he proclaimed this vision, but the crowd covered their ears, shouted loudly, and dragged him outside the city.

there they stoned stephen, while a young man named saul watched over the garments of those carrying out the execution. as he was dying, stephen prayed, "lord jesus, receive my spirit," and then asked, "lord, do not hold this sin against them." with these words, stephen peacefully died, becoming the first christian martyr.
story 52 (read acts 8 - 9) the conversion of saul (paul) day 52

after stephen's martyrdom, saul approved of his death, and a severe persecution broke out against the church in jerusalem. saul was ravaging the church by entering house after house; dragging off people, committing them to prison. determined to destroy the church, he obtained permission from the high priest to travel to damascus and arrest any followers of jesus he found there.

now as he was reaching damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him. he fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, "saul, saul, why do you persecute me?" he asked, "who are you, lord?" the reply came, "i am jesus, whom you are persecuting. but get up and enter the city, and you will be told what you are to do." the men who were traveling with him heard the voice but saw no one. saul got up from the ground, and though his eyes were open, he could see nothing so, they led him by the hand into damascus. for 3 days he was without sight, and neither ate nor drank.

now there was a disciple in damascus named ananias. the lord said to him, "get up and go to the house of judas, look for a man named saul. at this moment he is praying, and he has seen in a vision a man named ananias lay his hands on him so that he might regain his sight." although ananias was afraid because of saul's reputation for persecuting christians, god assured him that saul had been chosen to become his instrument to proclaim the gospel to the gentiles, kings, and the people of israel.

so, ananias went and entered the house. he laid his hands on saul and said, "brother saul, the lord jesus, who appeared to you on your way here, has sent me so that you may regain your sight and be filled with the holy spirit." and immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and his sight was restored. then he got up and was baptized and strengthened with food.

from that moment, saul's life was completely transformed. he was also known as paul & immediately began preaching about jesus. the people of damascus were astonished because the man who had once persecuted christians was now boldly proclaiming christ. saul became increasingly more powerful and confounded the jews who lived in damascus by proving that jesus was the messiah.
paul wrote 13 letters
each letter helped the people to live better & holy lives in jesus christ.
read each letter and allow god's grace & teachings to help you live holier lives.
letters of the other disciples
the book of revelation (part 1) story 53 (read revelation 1 - 12) day 53

jesus christ gave a revelation from god to his servant john to show what would soon take place. while in exile on the island of patmos, john received a vision of the glorified jesus, standing among seven golden lampstands. jesus appeared in great majesty, holding seven stars in his right hand, with eyes like blazing fire, a voice like many waters, and a face shining like the sun. his head and his hair were white as white wool, his feet were like burnished bronze. from, his mouth came a sword. overwhelmed, john fell at his feet, but jesus comforted him, declaring that he is the first and the last, the living one who died and now lives forever, holding the keys of death and hades. jesus commanded john to write down everything he saw and send it to the seven churches. ( rev 1 - 3)

john was invited by god to enter heaven, where he saw a glorious throne with god seated upon it in majesty. surrounding the throne were a brilliant rainbow, twenty - four elders wearing white robes and golden crowns, seven flaming torches representing the seven spirits of god, and a crystal - like sea. around the throne stood four living creatures, a lion, an ox, a man, and an eagle. they continually worshiped god, proclaiming, “holy, holy, holy is the lord god almighty.” whenever they praised god, the twenty - four elders fell down before his throne, laid their crowns before him, and worshiped him, declaring that he alone is worthy of all glory, honor, and power because he created all things and by his will everything exists. ( rev 4)

john saw a great sign in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head. she gave birth to a male child who was destined to rule all nations, but the child was taken safely to god and his throne. a great red dragon, with seven heads tried to destroy the child and then pursued the woman, but god protected her in the wilderness. ( rev 12)

a war broke out in heaven, where michael and his angels defeated the dragon and cast satan and his angels down to the earth. heaven rejoiced because satan had been overcome through the blood of the lamb and the faithful testimony of god's people. filled with anger, the dragon went to make war against all who keep god's commandments and remain faithful to jesus.
the book of revelation (part 2) story 54 (read revelation 13 - 22) day 54

john saw a terrifying beast rise out of the sea with 7 heads, 10 horns, and 10 crowns. it looked like a leopard, had feet like a bear, and a mouth like a lion. the dragon gave the beast his power, authority, and throne. the people of the earth began to marvel and worship both the dragon and the beast. the beast spoke blasphemies against god, persecuted god's people, and was given authority over the nations for a time. ( rev 13)

john then saw a second beast rise from the earth. it had two horns like a lamb but spoke like a dragon. this beast performed miraculous signs. it caused everyone to worship the first beast & to receive the mark of the beast on their right hand or forehead. without the mark no one could buy or sell. the chapter ends by calling for wisdom, revealing that the number of the beast is 666, the number of a man.

john then saw heaven opened, and jesus christ appeared riding a white horse as the faithful and true king. his eyes were like blazing fire, he wore many crowns, his robe was dipped in blood, he was called word of god. the armies of heaven followed him on white horses. jesus came to judge the nations with righteousness, and on his robe and thigh was written, "king of kings and lord of lords." ( rev 19)

then, john saw an angel standing in the sun, he called to all the birds that fly in midheaven, "come, gather for the great supper of god, to eat the flesh of kings, captains, horses and their riders & flesh of all." then i saw the beast and the kings of the earth with their armies gathered to make war against the rider on the horse and against his army.

the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image. these two were thrown alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur. the rest were killed by the sword of the rider on the horse, the sword that came from his mouth; and all the birds were gorged with their flesh.

then, john saw an angel coming down from heaven, holding the key to the bottomless pit and a great chain. he seized the dragon, that ancient serpent, who is the devil and satan, and bound him for a thousand years, threw him into the pit and locked and sealed it over him, so that he would deceive the nations no more, after that he must be let out for a little while. those who had remained faithful to jesus, refused to worship the beast, and had not received its mark were raised to life. they reigned with christ a 1000 years. this is the first resurrection & the 2 nd death had no power over them. ( rev 20)

after the thousand years, the dragon (satan) was released for a short time and deceived the nations once more, gathering them for battle against god's people. however, god sent fire from heaven to destroy them, and the dragon was thrown into the lake of fire, where the beast and the false prophet already were, to be punished forever.

john then saw the great white throne judgment, where all the dead stood before god and were judged according to what was written in the books. those whose names were not found in the book of life were thrown into the lake of fire, which is the second death.

john saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the old creation had passed away. he saw the new jerusalem coming down from heaven, shining with god's glory like a beautiful bride prepared for her husband. god declared that he would dwell with his people forever, wiping away every tear. there would be no more death, sorrow, crying, or pain, because all things had been made new. those who remain faithful would inherit eternal life, while those who rejected god would face the second death in the lake of fire. ( rev 21)

there was no temple, because the lord god almighty and the lamb are its temple. the city needed no sun or moon, for god's glory and the lamb were its light. only those whose names were written in the lamb's book of life would enter this perfect and eternal city. an angel then showed john the glorious holy city, new jerusalem, descending from heaven. the city had a great wall with twelve gates guarded by twelve angels, and twelve foundations bearing the names of the apostles. it was built of pure gold, clear as glass, with foundations decorated with precious jewels and gates made of single pearls.

john was shown the river of the water of life, flowing from the throne of god and the lamb through the middle of the new jerusalem. on both sides of the river stood the tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruit and leaves that bring healing to the nations. god himself would dwell with his people, he would be their everlasting light, and his servants would reign with him forever. ( rev 22)

the angel reminded john that these words are true and trustworthy, and jesus declared, “i am coming soon.” john fell down to worship the angel, but the angel told him to worship god alone. jesus identified himself as the alpha and the omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end, inviting all who are thirsty to receive the water of life freely. the book closes with a warning not to add to or take away from its prophecy, a promise that jesus will come again soon, and the final prayer of the church: “amen. come, lord jesus!”
